scoring.formula: For each category with applicable checks: normalized = category.max * earned / applicable_max. Total = sum(normalized) * 100 / sum(category.max for categories with applicable checks). Caps apply after normalization.
scoring.required: Always scored. A required check cannot be marked N/A.
scoring.recommended: Scored by default. It may be excluded only through configuration.excludedChecks with a written reason.
scoring.conditional: Scored only when configuration.optionalChecks enables its module; otherwise it is N/A and excluded from the denominator.
scoring.rounding: Category normalized values are rounded to 2 decimals. Total and final are rounded to 1 decimal. The display score is the final rounded to the nearest integer. Bands use the display score.
scoring.owner_data: Owner-data questions are never scored and never reduce the website score.
scoring.weaker_viewport: When a check lists mobile and desktop, the weaker viewport determines the score.

optionalModules.label: Multilingual access
optionalModules.description: Enable when the target market needs a language other than the primary site language. Configure preferredLanguages, for example ["en", "es"].

optionalModules.label: Text/SMS path
optionalModules.description: Enable when the business accepts texted leads or the market expects SMS.

optionalModules.label: Chat or callback request
optionalModules.description: Enable when a human-backed chat or callback channel is part of the intended lead mix.

optionalModules.label: After-hours or emergency path
optionalModules.description: Enable for emergency, restoration, HVAC, plumbing, pest, and similar trades. Disable for businesses that do not take urgent work.

optionalModules.label: License, insurance, and certifications
optionalModules.description: Enable where licensing or insurance is a meaningful buyer concern. It is scored only on visible claims.

optionalModules.label: Financing and payment path
optionalModules.description: High-ticket trades may benefit. It is an opportunity flag and owner-data question, not a universal score penalty.

optionalModules.label: Video or VSL
optionalModules.description: A video can help some offers, but its absence is not a revenue leak for every trade. Report it as an opportunity only.

optionalModules.label: Maintenance plan or membership
optionalModules.description: A continuity offer is valuable when the trade has recurring service needs. It is not a universal score requirement.

optionalModules.label: Tiered packages or premium option
optionalModules.description: Useful for some offers, irrelevant for others. Report as an opportunity, not a penalty.

optionalModules.label: Paid priority or same-day option
optionalModules.description: An optional revenue architecture choice. Report when it fits the trade and market.

optionalModules.label: Detailed price transparency
optionalModules.description: A price anchor is scored lightly in Understand. A full price list is optional and should be investigated, not assumed.

optionalModules.label: Content freshness
optionalModules.description: Fresh advice content can help search and trust, but it is not a universal revenue-leak penalty.

optionalModules.label: Named lead magnet
optionalModules.description: A named low-friction offer can help. Report as an opportunity when the current offer is only a generic free estimate.

optionalModules.label: Referral program
optionalModules.description: Public referral signals are sparse. Treat referral operations as an owner-data opportunity.

optionalModules.label: Paid traffic landing experience
optionalModules.description: Enable when ads are known to point at the site. Inspect landing-page relevance, CTA, phone/form, speed, mobile usability, and measurement. Never invent ad spend or performance.

items.title: Service clarity

anchors.4: The first viewport names the service in plain language on mobile and desktop. A homeowner can say what is sold without scrolling.
anchors.2: The service is named only after scrolling, or only in jargon or a brand slogan.
anchors.1: Brand name or slogan only; a visitor must guess what is sold.
anchors.0: Neither the service nor a recognizable category is visible on the page.

items.evidence: M-01, D-01; quote the hero copy
items.recommendedIntervention: Name the service in the hero in plain language.

items.title: Location and service-area clarity

anchors.3: The city or region, a service radius or area list, and one local proof signal are visible. A visitor can tell whether they are eligible.
anchors.2: A city is named, but the service area or local proof is missing.
anchors.1: Only a broad region or county is named, with no way to judge eligibility.
anchors.0: No location signal on the site.

items.evidence: Hero, footer, contact page, service-area page
items.recommendedIntervention: State the city/service area and add local proof.

items.title: Customer problem and outcome clarity

anchors.3: The page names the customer's problem, the outcome, and who it is for in specific language.
anchors.2: It names the problem or the outcome, but not both, or the customer is vague.
anchors.1: Generic quality claims only (family owned, best service, trusted).
anchors.0: No problem, outcome, or customer signal.

items.evidence: Hero, first scroll, service page intro
items.recommendedIntervention: Name the customer problem and the outcome.

items.title: Primary action clarity

anchors.3: One dominant next step is visible above the fold on mobile and desktop, and secondary actions do not compete with it.
anchors.2: The next step is visible on one viewport only, or two actions have equal visual weight.
anchors.1: The next step requires scrolling, or is buried among three or more competing actions.
anchors.0: No clear next step anywhere on the page.

items.recommendedIntervention: Use one dominant next step above the fold.

items.title: Offer specificity and price anchor

anchors.2: A named offer includes a price, starting-at price, or range.
anchors.1: A named offer exists, but there is no price or range.
anchors.0: No named offer, or only a generic free estimate.

items.recommendedIntervention: Add a starting-at price or range for a core job.

items.title: Service navigation

anchors.2: The main services are reachable in two taps or fewer, and at least one service page exists with relevant content.
anchors.1: Services are reachable in three taps, or only from a long menu with no dedicated pages.
anchors.0: No service navigation, or service links are broken.

items.evidence: Mobile menu, header nav, service pages
items.recommendedIntervention: Put the top services in the main navigation.

items.title: Service-area eligibility navigation

anchors.1: A service-area list, city page, map, or ZIP check lets a visitor confirm eligibility.
anchors.0: No way to confirm whether the visitor's location is served.

items.evidence: Service areas page, footer, contact page
items.recommendedIntervention: Add a service-area list, map, or ZIP check.

items.title: Language access

anchors.2: Every configured preferred language is reachable in two taps or fewer, with translated home and conversion pages.
anchors.1: A language notice or one translated page exists, but the conversion path is not translated or is hard to reach.
anchors.0: No visible access to a configured preferred language.

items.evidence: Mobile menu/footer first, then desktop; language switcher, /es/, hreflang, notice
items.principle: Language access; only scored when configured for the market
items.recommendedIntervention: Add the configured language path and translate conversion pages.

items.title: Phone visible and consistent

anchors.3: A phone number is visible on the home and contact pages, and the same number appears in both places.
anchors.2: A phone number is visible, but numbers differ or the contact page is missing it.
anchors.1: The number is buried in the footer or on one page only.
anchors.0: No phone number is visible.

items.recommendedIntervention: Use one visible phone number consistently.

items.title: Click-to-call on mobile

anchors.3: A working tel: link is visible in the header, hero, or sticky action bar.
anchors.1: A tel: link exists, but it is buried or only on a secondary page.
anchors.0: No tel: link; the phone is plain text.

items.recommendedIntervention: Make the mobile phone a tel: link in a persistent action.

items.title: Text/SMS path

anchors.1: A working sms: link is visible in a sensible lead path.
anchors.0: No sms: link, or the link is broken.

items.recommendedIntervention: Add a working sms: link when SMS is enabled.

items.title: Form exists and is reachable

anchors.3: A lead form is reachable in two taps or fewer from the home page and renders with visible fields.
anchors.2: A form exists but is buried, only on a secondary page, or only reachable from the footer.
anchors.1: Only an account-gated or third-party form exists.
anchors.0: No form anywhere on the site.

items.recommendedIntervention: Make the lead form reachable in two taps.

items.title: Form friction

anchors.3: Five or fewer fields, no account creation, and no irrelevant required fields.
anchors.2: Six to eight fields, or one unnecessary required field or account step.
anchors.1: Nine or more fields, multiple unnecessary required fields, or an account required before contact.
anchors.0: The form requires a lengthy intake, payment, or impossible information before a human can respond.

items.evidence: Count visible fields; list required fields
items.recommendedIntervention: Cut fields to name, phone, ZIP, and problem.

items.title: Form usability

anchors.3: Labels are visible, inputs use correct types and autocomplete, validation is understandable, and the submit control is reachable on mobile.
anchors.1: One usability problem: a missing label, wrong input type, no autocomplete, or a submit button that requires extra scrolling.
anchors.0: Two or more problems, or the submit control is not reachable.

items.recommendedIntervention: Add labels, input types, autocomplete, and a reachable submit.

items.title: Online scheduler or booking

anchors.3: A working scheduler with live availability is reachable in two taps or fewer and usable on mobile.
anchors.2: A scheduler exists, but it takes extra steps, requires an account, or is confusing on mobile.
anchors.1: Only an appointment-request form exists; no live availability.
anchors.0: No scheduler or booking path.

items.evidence: Book/quote path trace; do not submit
items.recommendedIntervention: Add a working scheduler with live availability.

items.title: No conversion dead end

anchors.2: Every high-intent page (home, service, about, contact) ends with a clear next step or persistent action.
anchors.1: Some high-intent pages end without a next step.
anchors.0: High-intent pages routinely end with no action, or the primary action is broken.

items.evidence: End of each crawled high-intent page
items.recommendedIntervention: End every high-intent page with a next step.

items.title: Chat or callback request

anchors.1: A human-backed chat, callback request, or equivalent alternate channel is visible and does not block the page.
anchors.0: No alternate channel, or only a dead bot.

items.evidence: Widget inspection; do not send a message
items.recommendedIntervention: Add a human-backed chat or callback when enabled.

items.title: Response and acknowledgement promise

anchors.3: An explicit promise states the response time, channel, and hours (for example, 'We call back within 15 minutes, 7am-7pm').
anchors.2: An explicit response time is stated, but the channel or hours are missing.
anchors.1: Only vague language ('we will be in touch soon').
anchors.0: No acknowledgement or response expectation.

items.evidence: Form area, contact page, confirmation copy
items.recommendedIntervention: Publish a response time, channel, and hours.

items.title: After-hours or emergency path

anchors.2: Hours plus an after-hours or emergency path (phone, form, or explicit next step) are visible.
anchors.1: Hours are visible, but there is no after-hours or emergency path.
anchors.0: Neither hours nor an after-hours path is visible.

items.recommendedIntervention: State hours and the after-hours or emergency path.

items.title: Booking path steps and mobile usability

anchors.3: Book or quote is reachable in two taps or fewer and completes without an account or confusing third-party transition.
anchors.2: Three taps, or one unnecessary step or confusing transition.
anchors.1: Four or more taps, or a dead end that requires the visitor to start over.
anchors.0: The booking path is broken or cannot be completed.

items.evidence: Mobile path trace; no appointment selected
items.recommendedIntervention: Reduce booking steps and keep the path on-site.

items.title: Confirmation expectations

anchors.2: The page states what happens after submission and when, including a confirmation channel.
anchors.1: Generic 'we will contact you' language only.
anchors.0: No confirmation or next-step expectation.

items.evidence: Form area, booking page, confirmation copy
items.recommendedIntervention: State what happens after submission and when.

items.title: Qualification context without over-asking

anchors.3: The flow captures the service, ZIP or service area, problem, and a contact preference without asking for irrelevant or excessive data.
anchors.2: The flow captures enough to route the lead but misses one useful field.
anchors.1: The flow captures too little to route the job, or too much before a human can respond.
anchors.0: No usable qualification path.

items.evidence: Form fields, quote flow, service page FAQs
items.recommendedIntervention: Capture service, ZIP or area, problem, and contact preference.

items.title: Estimate or quote request workflow

anchors.3: A clear estimate request captures scope and offers a sensible next step (upload, photos, or scheduling) without forcing a full intake.
anchors.2: A quote request or contact form exists, but scope or next step is unclear.
anchors.1: Phone-only estimate request with no visible form or path.
anchors.0: No estimate or quote path.

items.recommendedIntervention: Add an estimate request with scope and a clear next step.

items.title: Review volume, source, and profile link

anchors.4: A rating, review count, named external source, and a link that opens the review profile are visible; 50+ reviews at 4.5+.
anchors.2: A rating and count are visible, but the count is under 50 or there is no external review-platform link.
anchors.1: Three to ten handwritten testimonials, with no aggregate rating or source.
anchors.0: No reviews, testimonials, or proof.

items.recommendedIntervention: Show rating, count, source, and a profile link.

items.title: Specific testimonials and case studies

anchors.3: Three or more stories include a name or photo, job type, and a specific outcome.
anchors.2: One or two specific stories.
anchors.1: Generic quotes only.
anchors.0: No testimonials or case studies.

items.evidence: Reviews page, service pages, case studies
items.recommendedIntervention: Add named stories with job type and outcome.

items.title: Real project proof

anchors.2: Five or more real job photos, with captions, location, or before/after context.
anchors.1: Stock photos, or an uncaptioned gallery with no job context.
anchors.0: No project photos.

items.recommendedIntervention: Caption real job photos with city, job, and result.

items.title: License, insurance, and certifications

anchors.2: A license number, an insurance or bond statement, and a relevant certification are visible.
anchors.1: One of the three is visible.
anchors.0: None is visible. Do not infer legitimacy from an absent badge.

items.recommendedIntervention: Show license, insurance, and relevant certifications.

items.title: Guarantee and warranty specificity

anchors.2: A specific workmanship or material guarantee with a term and scope is visible near the buying path.
anchors.1: The word guarantee or warranty appears, but the term or scope is missing, or it is buried in the footer.
anchors.0: No guarantee or warranty signal.

items.recommendedIntervention: State the warranty term and scope.

items.title: Identity and differentiation consistency

anchors.2: A real owner or team identity and one verifiable differentiator appear consistently across the site.
anchors.1: One of the two is present, or the identity is inconsistent across pages.
anchors.0: Neither is present, or the business identity changes between pages.

items.evidence: About page, hero, footer, contact page
items.recommendedIntervention: Use one identity and one verifiable differentiator.

items.title: Mobile LCP

anchors.4: Median mobile LCP is at or under 2.5 seconds.
anchors.2: Median mobile LCP is 2.5 to 4.0 seconds.
anchors.0: Median mobile LCP is over 4.0 seconds.

items.evidence: Lighthouse mobile, median of at least three runs
items.recommendedIntervention: Compress the hero and defer non-critical scripts.

items.title: Mobile layout usability

anchors.4: No horizontal overflow, readable body text, no clipped conversion controls, and the menu opens.
anchors.2: One layout problem that does not block the primary action.
anchors.1: Two layout problems, or one that makes the primary action hard to use.
anchors.0: Three or more problems, or the mobile experience is unusable.

items.recommendedIntervention: Fix viewport, text size, clipping, and menu usability.

items.title: Tap targets and persistent action

anchors.3: Primary tap targets are at least 44px and a call/book action is persistently reachable.
anchors.2: Targets are mostly adequate, but the primary action requires scrolling back to the top.
anchors.1: Small targets and a buried primary action.
anchors.0: The primary action is not usable on mobile.

items.recommendedIntervention: Use 44px targets and a persistent action.

items.title: HTTPS and security

anchors.1: The site loads over HTTPS with a valid certificate and no unrelated redirect.
anchors.0: HTTP only, a certificate failure, or a suspicious redirect.

items.recommendedIntervention: Serve HTTPS with a valid certificate.

items.title: Broken links, CTAs, and conversion-blocking errors

anchors.3: No conversion-blocking broken links, CTAs, forms, or JavaScript errors observed.
anchors.2: A non-blocking broken link or script error exists, but the primary path still works.
anchors.1: One primary path is broken, but another contact path works.
anchors.0: Multiple conversion paths are broken, or the primary path is a dead end.

items.evidence: Link/CTA trace, console errors, scheduler state
items.recommendedIntervention: Fix broken links, CTAs, forms, and conversion-blocking errors.

items.title: Title, meta description, and H1

anchors.3: Title, meta description, and H1 each combine the primary service and city.
anchors.2: Two of the three combine service and city.
anchors.1: One of the three does.
anchors.0: None does, or the home page has no H1.

items.recommendedIntervention: Put service and city in title, meta, and H1.

items.title: Indexability

anchors.2: A canonical is present, robots rules allow the page, and a sitemap is reachable.
anchors.1: One of the three is missing or ambiguous.
anchors.0: The page is noindexed or blocked by robots, or no indexable page is reachable.

items.recommendedIntervention: Fix canonical, robots, and sitemap.

items.title: Local schema and NAP consistency

anchors.2: LocalBusiness or Service schema is present and the visible name, address, and phone are consistent.
anchors.1: One of the two is present.
anchors.0: Neither is present, or the visible NAP conflicts across pages.

items.recommendedIntervention: Add LocalBusiness or Service schema and consistent NAP.

items.title: Service and location pages with unique content

anchors.1: At least one service page and one location or service-area page contain unique, useful local content.
anchors.0: Only a list of cities, duplicated pages, or no service/location depth.

items.recommendedIntervention: Build unique service and location pages.

items.title: Analytics present

anchors.2: GA4, Google Tag Manager, or an equivalent analytics platform is loaded on the public pages.
anchors.1: Some analytics or pixel is present, but no general analytics platform is detectable.
anchors.0: No analytics signal detected.

items.recommendedIntervention: Install GA4, GTM, or an equivalent analytics platform.

items.title: Conversion and paid-traffic measurement

anchors.2: Conversion events plus a call/form tracking or ads tag are detectable.
anchors.1: One signal is detectable (for example, Google Ads or Meta Pixel only).
anchors.0: No conversion or paid-traffic measurement signal is detectable.

items.principle: Measurement; absence is a signal, not proof of broken attribution
items.recommendedIntervention: Add conversion events and ads or call tracking.

ownerData.title: Speed-to-lead
ownerData.whyItMatters: A fast first response is often the difference between a booked job and a competitor's job. The public site cannot prove response time.
questions: What is the median time from lead to first human response?
How does that change by lead source (call, form, chat, text, ads)?
Who owns new leads during business hours and after hours?
How many contact attempts are made before a lead is abandoned?
How many inbound calls are missed or abandoned each week?

ownerData.title: After-hours and emergency handling
ownerData.whyItMatters: Emergency demand does not wait for office hours. A visible emergency path is not proof that a human answers it.
questions: What happens to a call or form submitted after hours?
Is there an on-call rotation or answering service?
What percentage of after-hours leads become jobs?
Are emergency jobs priced or prioritized differently?

ownerData.title: Lead quality and routing
ownerData.whyItMatters: A form can collect data and still fail to route the right job to the right person.
questions: Which form fields are actually used to qualify or route a lead?
What percentage of form leads are spam, out of area, or the wrong service?
Where do form leads land, and who sees them?
What information is missing most often when the office calls back?

ownerData.title: Booking capacity and confirmation
ownerData.whyItMatters: An online booking can create a bad customer experience if the calendar is wrong or the office cannot absorb the slot.
questions: How many booked jobs are rescheduled or cancelled each week?
Is the online calendar connected to real crew capacity?
Who confirms appointments, and when?
What happens when the requested slot is unavailable?

ownerData.title: Estimate pipeline
ownerData.whyItMatters: Open estimates are often the largest recoverable revenue pool. The website cannot show how many exist.
questions: How many estimates are currently open?
What is the total value of open estimates?
What is the average time from request to estimate delivered?
What percentage of estimates are accepted?
What percentage of estimate requests never receive an estimate?

ownerData.title: Estimate close rate by source and size
ownerData.whyItMatters: The same website can produce very different revenue depending on close rate, job size, and lead source.
questions: What is the close rate by lead source?
What is the close rate by job size or service line?
What is the average job value?
Which objections appear most often on estimates?
Which lost reasons are recorded?

ownerData.title: Estimate follow-up
ownerData.whyItMatters: Unclosed estimates are a high-value opportunity that a public website audit cannot observe.
questions: What percentage of open estimates receive follow-up?
How quickly is the first follow-up made?
How many attempts are made before follow-up stops?
Which channels are used (call, text, email)?
Are estimates segmented by size, service, or age?
Are stale estimates reactivated on a schedule?

ownerData.title: Customer history and job completion
ownerData.whyItMatters: Repeat and referral revenue depends on knowing who bought, what was installed, and when the next service is due.
questions: How many past customers are in the CRM?
Is job history, equipment age, and service date recorded?
Is there a post-job check-in?
How many customers buy a second service within 12 months?

ownerData.title: Review requests
ownerData.whyItMatters: A strong review profile is public, but the review-request process is not.
questions: Are customers automatically asked for a review?
How soon after the job is the ask made?
Is the ask sent by SMS, email, or in person?
Is the process measured by technician or job type?
Is negative feedback captured before it becomes a public review?

ownerData.title: Referral operations
ownerData.whyItMatters: Referrals are often the lowest-cost lead source, but they are rarely visible on the website.
questions: Do you ask for referrals? When and how?
Is there a referral offer or tracking method?
What percentage of new customers come from referrals?
Are referral partners (realtors, property managers, adjacent trades) tracked?
Is referral follow-up owned by someone?

ownerData.title: Reactivation and repeat business
ownerData.whyItMatters: Old leads, unsold estimates, and inactive customers can produce revenue without new ad spend.
questions: How many past customers are inactive for 12+ months?
How many unsold estimates are older than 30, 60, or 90 days?
Are seasonal services or maintenance visits scheduled automatically?
Is there a maintenance plan or membership list?
Has anyone contacted the inactive list in the last year?

ownerData.title: Marketing attribution and channel profitability
ownerData.whyItMatters: Tags can show that traffic arrived; only business data can show which channel produces closed revenue.
questions: Is lead source recorded on every lead and job?
Can you report cost per lead, cost per booked job, and cost per closed job by channel?
Do you know revenue by channel?
Which campaigns produced jobs in the last 90 days?
How much is spent on ads, and what is the return?
